@graph.headline: Net Expectancy: Your Edge After Everything
@graph.description: Open your broker statement and audit your edge line by line: rank the cost that kills it, price the monthly frequency drag, and decide what to change.

mainEntity.name: How do I work out net expectancy from my journal for this audit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Take total net P&L after all charges and divide by the number of completed trades. Open positions are excluded — they have not finished. A trade that is breakeven before costs but negative after costs enters the total at its actual negative net amount after costs, not at ₹0.

mainEntity.name: No single cost line is large, yet my net expectancy is at or below zero. What do I change?

acceptedAnswer.text: The gross edge itself is too thin for any realistic cost load. Follow Step 5's last row: the lever is the system — a larger gross edge, or a different setup altogether.

mainEntity.name: My charges are not flat per trade. How do I rank them?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use the average-cost-per-trade bridge from Step 1: average cost per trade = total costs ÷ number of completed trades, taken from the statement. Flag it for what it is — an average, not a per-trade constant — then split the lines and rank them largest first.

mainEntity.name: How do I read a low fill rate alongside net expectancy?

acceptedAnswer.text: Report the fill rate next to your net expectancy, as in Step 4: setups spotted versus fills taken over the same period for the same setup. A low fill rate changes the diagnosis — the problem may be execution and fill discipline rather than the setup's gross edge — and you cannot tell which until you log both numbers.
